items.title: Mrs. Francis Oliver Interview, 1969-05-10
items.q: I went out to see some musicians like Kid Ory

ctx.x: He went over to Biloxi until I think he was maybe seventeen or nineteen, something like twenty or something I don't know, I don't know how old he was But I mean the last time I saw him, the first time I ever saw him, to remember him He was in Biloxi with my aunt, Hortense was her name Hortense? Yeah, they called Hortense H-O-R? Hortense, H-O-R-T-E-N-S-E-S-E-S-E-S-E-S…

When I was out there in 1940, and your brother was still living in New York, I'd seen him before, but I went out to see some musicians like Kid Ory and another old-time guitar player, his nickname was Gigi Williams, Norwood Williams. He lived down in Watts. I remember hearing him speak of Gigi. He was running a filling station, and he told me, he said, he thought it was, he said, Jelly Roll's mother. He didn't know it was his godmother. He said, his mother lives over here in Watts. It was his godfather. It was…

died about that time. Yes. That's when he went out. Eddie Hunter and Lolly Hunter. That was his godmother. His godfather. So I didn't get to meet him. But I mean, Lolly was so crazy about my mother that she wanted to take all three of us to register, and my grandmother wanted us to be a red Catholic, see, so she wouldn't let us go. And to what good does it do to hand down religion before a child is old enough to know what they're doing? You know what I mean? I didn't do that with my son. I mean, he, I christened…
